clue.text: Money in Stock Exchange collapse runs out

indicators.note: out signals that the runs are dropped from the collapse word

parts.note: a crash is a sudden collapse in share prices
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Cash is running out after a stock market crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Cash is ready money in notes and coins, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Whip a professional soldier losing heart under pressure

indicators.note: under places the soldier below the pressure letter in this down answer

parts.note: pro is short for professional
P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter is dropped

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranking soldier

explanation.surface: A trained soldier, fainthearted under strain, is flogged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' looks like flogging, but it is slang for steal; PRIVATE loses its central V to give PRIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip something is British slang for stealing it, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: Plant mentioned in Black Beauty?

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so we go by the sound

parts.note: the novel Black Beauty is a tale about a horse

explanation.surface: A plant named in the classic horse novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Horsetail is a rush-like plant of the genus Equisetum.

clue.text: Anti-social type dropping his habit?

parts.note: reads like a monk or nun quitting the order, but the habit is a bad custom: someone who habitually drops rubbish in the street

explanation.surface: A loner who has given up his habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' suggests a religious robe being dropped; in fact the anti-social habit is dropping rubbish, so the type is the one who drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: A British term for someone who carelessly scatters rubbish in public places.

clue.text: French writer needing no introduction in Los Angeles theatre

indicators.note: in puts the shortened writer inside the city letters
needing no introduction means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Blaise Pascal was a French writer and philosopher

explanation.surface: A famous French author appears unannounced at a Hollywood playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala is the celebrated opera house in Milan.

clue.text: Wife gets awfully neurotic staying in bad hotels in part of Europe

indicators.note: staying in puts the wife and her jumbled word inside the other group
bad shows the letters of hotels are spoilt into a new order
awfully signals that the following word is badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A wife becomes dreadfully anxious while lodging in poor hotels on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neurotic' looks like it describes the wife, and 'bad hotels' like the complaint, but both are anagram fodder, with 'gets' only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Low Countries are the Netherlands, Belgium and Luxembourg, a region of north-west Europe.

clue.text: Mistake by Latin scholar, having transcribed "terra" with neuter ending

indicators.note: transcribed suggests copying out with the letters jumbled

parts.note: -um is the neuter ending of Latin adjectives such as bonum

explanation.surface: A classicist makes a slip copying out the Latin word for earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratum is the Latin word for an error, used especially for a printing mistake.

clue.text: Fragrance of flower, say

indicators.note: say means as it is spoken

parts.note: in crosswords a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Oder

explanation.surface: The scent of a bloom, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but a river; the Oder runs between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a smell, and a pleasant one is a fragrance.

clue.text: Not so fast

parts.note: a call to slow down, read against a word for doing a hundred miles an hour on a motorbike; reversing the opening word up the column also fits

explanation.walkthrough: TON-UP means reaching 100mph, so 'not so fast' is ironic; read upwards in the grid, TON gives NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton-up is British slang for a speed of a hundred miles per hour.

clue.text: Casual clothes unusual in war posters

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of the next words are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: Leisure garments that are an odd sight on wartime posters.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing designed for sport is widely worn as relaxed everyday dress.

clue.text: Short period of time, right before noon

definitions.text: Short period of time, right before noon

indicators.note: before places the right letter ahead of the noon letter

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a brief while

explanation.surface: A brief spell just ahead of midday.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a poetic word for the morning, the time just before noon, and 'Short' because it is shorter than the full word.
explanation.definitionFit: Morn is a literary clipped form of morning, the hours leading up to midday.

clue.text: Fellow takes a long time going round wine store

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap

indicators.note: going round tells us the long-time word turns back on itself

parts.note: an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A man takes ages to walk round a wine shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or shop selling wine.

clue.text: Beat away team in this?

parts.note: out means away, as in 'she is out'
a strip is the kit a sports team plays in

explanation.surface: A side is beaten while playing away in its kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The away team plays in its away kit; British football calls a team's kit its strip.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip someone is to outdo or surpass them, so to beat them.

clue.text: South American film director working for a spell

parts.note: Incan describes the Incas of Peru
Jacques Tati was a French film director
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A Latin American film-maker at work for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' suggests a period of time, but it is a magic formula.
explanation.definitionFit: An incantation is a chanted magic formula, a spell.

clue.text: Killer transported in motor car

indicators.note: something transported in a vehicle is carried inside it, so the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A murderer is carried off in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: An orca is the killer whale, so 'killer' alone is a crossword shorthand for it.

clue.text: Partner's very clever, getting shed replaced by civil engineer

indicators.note: replaced by tells us one run of letters is swapped out for another

parts.note: accomplished means highly skilled
the word shed taken as written

explanation.surface: A partner of great skill loses a garden shed to an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: Partner's means 'Partner is', so the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplice is a partner, especially in crime.

clue.text: Indeed, with flowers on head, appears relaxed

indicators.note: on head places the flowers on top of the other word in this down answer

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
surely means certainly, indeed

explanation.surface: Wearing a floral garland, someone looks laid-back indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely means unhurried and relaxed.

clue.text: Offer support, providing some ammunition after a series of shots

indicators.note: after puts the ammunition word behind the series word

parts.note: a rally is a long exchange of shots in tennis
a round is a single cartridge or shell

explanation.surface: Backing given by supplying ammunition after a volley of gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shots' suggests gunfire alongside the ammunition, but it is a tennis exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally round is an idiom for gathering to help someone in trouble.

clue.text: Food that's filled boy in French town briefly

indicators.note: in puts the boy inside the shortened town
briefly means the last letter is cut

parts.note: Rouen is a city in Normandy
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A dish stuffed with a youngster in a French town.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a rolled dish with a filling, such as meat or sponge.

clue.text: Rejects Democrat's wishes

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
itches are cravings or desires

explanation.surface: A party member's desires are turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: To ditch is to discard or reject something.

clue.text: Places to stay, fashionable quarters

parts.note: in means trendy, as in 'the in crowd'
north and south are two quarters of the compass, N and S

explanation.surface: Lodgings that are trendy accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' looks like part of the definition (lodgings), but it gives two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are hotels or pubs offering rooms for travellers.

clue.text: Fellow had not finished sandwich, having swallowed a nut

indicators.note: having swallowed puts the letter A inside the other pieces

parts.note: he'd is a contraction of 'he had', the fellow being 'he'

indicators.note: not finished means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: butty is a British slang word for a sandwich

explanation.surface: A man left his sandwich unfinished after choking on a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' looks like food, but as a verb it means to strike with the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To nut someone is British slang for striking them with the forehead.

clue.text: It is placed round, base of pot to support house plant

indicators.note: to support places the other pieces under the house letters in this down answer
is placed round tells us the it letters go around another letter

parts.note: it means sex appeal, SA

indicators.note: base of picks the last letter of pot

explanation.surface: A pot plant stands under the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosta is a leafy garden plant, also called plantain lily.

clue.text: In the past monarch got in difficulties

indicators.note: got in puts the monarch inside the past word

parts.note: ago means in the past
GR is George Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Long ago the king got into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for trouble or aggravation.

clue.text: President listened to loyal staff

indicators.note: listened to means we go by how the words sound

parts.note: a true man is a loyal member of staff

explanation.surface: A head of state heeds his faithful aides.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Truman was the 33rd President of the United States.

clue.text: Lengthy tale is the reverse of something entertaining

indicators.note: the reverse of tells us the fun phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a gas is informal for something great fun

explanation.surface: A long story is anything but entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface says the tale is dull; the reverse is literal: A GAS read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, originally a Norse heroic narrative.

clue.text: Rich mate's tight with it, being kind of mean

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A wealthy friend is stingy with money, being a sort of miser.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich mate's is 'Rich mate is'; 'tight' and 'mean' both suggest stinginess, but mean is the statistical average.
explanation.definitionFit: The arithmetic mean is the ordinary average, one kind of mean in statistics.

clue.text: A reflective work — written piece — about love as an ideal

indicators.note: reflective means mirrored, so the work is read backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: about puts the written piece around the love letter

parts.note: a thesis is a long written dissertation
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A thoughtful essay about love as a perfect state.
explanation.definitionFit: An apotheosis is the highest ideal or perfect example of something.

clue.text: Pull rabbit out of warren at last

indicators.note: out of here means outside of, the chatter word going round the letter

parts.note: to rabbit and to yak are both British slang for chatter

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of warren

explanation.surface: A magician tugs a rabbit from its burrow at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is a verb: in British slang to rabbit on is to talk endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull sharply.
